title: Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data
gist: Airbnb's CASTLE generates synthetic natural-language search queries and relevance labels jointly from de-identified booking sessions (booked vs viewed-but-unbooked listings), cutting KL divergence vs real queries 9.2x relative to Promptagator. A LinkedIn exchange flags that leakage-robust split comparisons were not reported.

insights.claim: Airbnb's CASTLE framework tackles the cold-start problem in natural language search by using de-identified booking sessions and LLMs to jointly generate synthetic search queries and relevance labels, enabling model training before enough real search traffic exists.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Proprietary behavioral data (bookings) is the moat that makes synthetic training data realistic; marketplaces with rich transaction logs can launch NL search faster.

insights.claim: CASTLE builds contrastive listing pairs where a booked listing is the positive and a viewed-but-unbooked listing is the negative, then prompts an LLM to write a query matching the positive but not the negative, so relevance labels come from construction rather than a separate judging step.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: A reusable recipe for any marketplace with view/purchase logs to bootstrap search relevance models.

insights.claim: Prior approaches such as InPars and Promptagator treat query generation and relevance labeling separately, which according to Airbnb's researchers introduces extra error and a gap between synthetic and real-user query distributions.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Joint generation-plus-labeling may supersede two-stage synthetic data pipelines in retrieval training.
insights.locator: Previous approaches, including InPars and Promptagator

insights.claim: CASTLE combines template prompts, few-shot prompts seeded with about 500 queries from targeted user research, and attribute-grounded prompts, and uses an LLM-based Virtual Judge to label pairs lacking booking history such as new listings; a CASTLE-R variant targets production once real traffic accumulates.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Small human seed sets plus LLM amplification can substitute for large labeled corpora.
insights.locator: The framework combines three query-generation strategies

insights.claim: CASTLE's synthetic queries reached a KL divergence of 1.01 against real-user query distributions versus 9.33 for the best baseline Promptagator, a 9.2-fold reduction, and 0.08 at attribute-type level versus 0.09 for manually curated survey seed queries.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Synthetic query realism is approaching human-curated quality, lowering the cost of launching LLM-powered search.

insights.claim: Three independent subject matter experts reviewing 200 sampled triplets agreed with CASTLE's relevance assignments 91% to 93% of the time.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: High human agreement suggests construction-based labels are usable for production training.
insights.locator: The researchers also conducted a human evaluation

insights.claim: Airbnb's CASTLE paper does not report a controlled comparison between random train/eval splits and stricter splits with disjoint seed templates and listing IDs, leaving possible template or listing leakage untested, though the team says it used untouched real queries and leakage guardrails.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Treat headline synthetic-data gains with some caution until leakage-robust splits are reported.
insights.locator: The evaluation methodology also prompted discussion on LinkedIn
